arjun: Heads-up: need a clear onboarding handshake for Private deployments. Two gaps spotted: (1) secret/credential surface (who rotates what), (2) rollback semantics when we remove a feature from hosted but private still has it. Thoughts?
maya: For secrets: prefer ephemeral signed delegation tokens rather than sharing static creds. short TTL + aud claim.
oliver: Ephemeral tokens are good but watch replay and clock skew. Also we need a revocation path: if private is compromised we must be able to revoke before TTL.
clara: Revocation can be handled by a revocation list in the control plane + short TTL. But private offline/offgrid customers are tricky.
noah: Offline private: we should support two modes: online-managed (control plane issues tokens + revocation) and self-managed (customer KMS; we only trust signed manifests).
arjun: That matches my thinking. For self-managed, we can't revoke mid-flight, so manifest versioning becomes the safety net. If we push a breaking change, private must opt-in.
maya: Example manifest vignette: ```yaml
manifest_version: 2
capabilities: [chat, embeddings, streaming]
handshake_key_id: hk-2026-01
signed_by: controlplane
issued_at: 2026-03-01T18:00:00Z
expires_at: 2026-03-02T18:00:00Z
```
Use signed manifest plus HSM-backed signature on our side.
oliver: Also include a "compatibility_vector" with minimal runtime reqs (kv_cache, max_seq_len, quant_mode) so the runtime can reject at startup. That prevents mysterious runtime fallbacks.
ops-bot: Buildkite: private-handshake-e2e started (job #4521) :rocket:
noah: Rollback semantics: if hosted removes feature X, how do we avoid private serving stale behavior? Options: feature-gates + deprecation windows.
clara: We should require a deprecation manifest with timelines. When hosted toggles feature off, control plane emits a deprecation_notice containing last_supported_version and cutoff_ts. Private must either migrate or explicitly set "compat_grace_period" in their manifest.
maya: Also expose a probe endpoint that returns "declared_capabilities" and a minimal health vector. Hosted can probe before routing traffic to private.
arjun: Good. That ties into our fallback flow too — don't optimistic-route for features that are declared-incompatible.
oliver: Security note: telemetry must not leak private tenant IDs. Mask or hash IDs in traces when crossing into hosted. Use ephemeral correlated IDs that map in control plane only.
noah: For rollback playbook: 1) if hosted finds incompatibility, flag customer, 2) enter coordination channel, 3) freeze requests to the mismatched feature with a "compat-fallback" that returns graceful error, 4) allow customer to opt into compatibility shim for a bounded window.
clara: We should codify the opt-in shim as an adapter plugin with a limited lifecycle and strict resource caps. No permanent shims.
maya: Tests: add handshake fuzz tests, offline manifest verification (stale clock), and revocation propagation test. Ops-bot, can you schedule a weekly run?
ops-bot: Scheduled: handshake-fuzz (daily), manifest-verification (weekly) :white_check_mark:
arjun: Decision summary: adopt signed manifests + ephemeral tokens for online mode; self-managed uses signed manifests + KMS responsibility; add compatibility_vector in manifest; require deprecation manifests for hosted-driven removals; restrict opt-in shims and add revocation + probe endpoints. Action owners: Maya (tokens + revocation), Oliver (compat_vector + probes), Clara (rollback playbook doc), Noah (tests + CI). Sync Thurs 11am to draft RFC.
noah: I'll start an RFC draft and link in this thread. thanks all. :v:
